reflections: Some weeks the reading queue runs dry — and that's its own kind of signal. The past month's newsletters dove deep into geopolitical feedback loops, cybersecurity's trust paradoxes, and the convergence of AI with human judgment. This week, with a house offer hanging in the balance and an on-call rotation demanding constant alertness, maybe the silence in the reading list mirrors the kind of week where life itself is the text you're reading most closely. The spring air is warm, the stakes feel real, and sometimes the most honest newsletter is the one that says: we were too busy living to curate. Next week, the queue refills. For now, be present.

fun_section.title: And Finally… Houses That Would Make Any Offer Rejection Sting Less
fun_section.content: Feeling stressed about house offers? At least you're not bidding on South Korea's Toilet House — a home shaped like a giant toilet where the bathroom walls are glass (press a button and they fog up, thankfully). Or Poland's Crooked House, which looks like a cartoon building mid-sneeze. Meanwhile in Sweden, the Mirrorcube Treehouse is covered entirely in mirrors so it disappears into the forest — good luck getting that one inspected. And Pennsylvania has a house shaped like a giant boot, because apparently someone read 'There Was an Old Woman Who Lived in a Shoe' and thought: yes, that's a floor plan. Ask Elsie which weird house she'd want to live in tonight at dinner.
